strings.name: Nadiem Makarim
strings.role: Gojek co-founder and former Indonesian education minister
strings.summary: Nadiem Makarim is an Indonesian entrepreneur and former minister. He co-founded Gojek, bringing motorcycle transport and delivery into app-based services, and oversaw education from 2019 to 2024. He promoted Merdeka Belajar reforms. After leaving office, he was convicted in the Chromebook procurement case; following a reduced sentence on appeal in 2026, he sought Supreme Court review.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Company formation, app launch, ministerial titles and policy outcomes are distinguished. Court rulings, his denial of wrongdoing and the subsequent cassation request remain separate; no final outcome is asserted.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Gojek, advancing Indonesia’s digital mobility and everyday-service platform and contributing to public education reform discussions.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Brown class of 2006; BA in international relations and Harvard Business School MBA. The disputed MBA graduation year is omitted.
strings.facts.f2.label: Ministerial service
strings.facts.f2.value: Education and Culture minister from October 23, 2019; Education, Culture, Research and Technology minister from April 28, 2021 until 2024.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Local digital services platform
strings.highlights.h1.text: Gojek began with motorcycle transport and courier services, expanding into a multi-service platform connecting consumers, drivers and merchants.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Merdeka Belajar education policy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Introduced reforms to examinations, lesson planning and admissions. Announcing policy does not establish independently verified learning gains.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Files Supreme Court cassation memorandum
strings.timeline.t1.text: ANTARA, citing his lawyer, reports a request to quash the appeal ruling and acquit him; no subsequent ruling has been verified.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Appeal reduces primary prison term to nine years
strings.timeline.t2.text: The Chromebook procurement corruption sentence fell from ten to nine years; he denies wrongdoing. Default imprisonment for nonpayment is not added directly to the primary term.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes minister with expanded responsibilities
strings.timeline.t3.text: Sworn in as Education, Culture, Research and Technology minister, continuing in the 2019–2024 cabinet.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Launches first Merdeka Belajar package
strings.timeline.t4.text: Covers school examinations, national assessment, simpler lesson plans and admissions zoning.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Moves from business to government
strings.timeline.t5.text: Announced departure from Gojek on October 21 and became Education and Culture minister on October 23; he is no longer described as its current CEO.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Gojek app launches
strings.timeline.t6.text: The company launches its app in Indonesia, bringing existing transport and delivery services onto a mobile platform.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-founds Gojek
strings.timeline.t7.text: Starts with motorcycle transport and courier services; company formation predates the app launch.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes undergraduate education at Brown
strings.timeline.t8.text: The university newsletter identifies him as class of 2006; SEAMEO’s CV confirms a BA in international relations.
